Scope The scope for TS 38.508 is suggested as: “The present document defines the test environment for the 5G System. This specification covers all aspects, including NG-RAN, 5GC and interworking between 5GS and EPS used for conformance tests of User Equipment (UE).” Some chapters will address similar issues as in TS 36.508 [1]. It’s suggested to reuse the heading 1 numbering for • Common test environment • Test environment for RF test • Test environment for Signalling test • Test environment for RRM tests Within common test environment, it’s suggested to reuse the following heading 2 and 3 numbering for • Environmental conditions • Common requirements of test equipment • Reference test conditions • Test frequencies • Radio conditions • Physical channel allocations • Signal levels • Physica

[3] (ran5_tdoc_chunks R5-204951, sim=0.5584)
During RAN5#87-e there was an email discussion about scope, purpose and drafting guideline for TS 38.522, but no formal agreement was achieved. Moreover no agreement could be reached on how to handle“Tested Bands” column and “Branch” column at RAN5#87-e, the disagreement is essentially about Scope, Purpose and drafting guideline for 38.522, such as what information shall be put in TS 38.522 and how to put the information in TS 38.522. This paper highlights the scope and purpose of 38.522 according to the current definition in 38.522 (Scope in section 1 & definition of each column in the beginning of section 4), proposes to correct some corresponding incorrect or ambiguous content in 38.522, and also provides some drafting guidelines for TS 38.522. TS 38.522 V16.4.0

The study is nearing its planned end date. Discussions now centre on Objective 2 (new formats) and Objective 3 (version control and repository solutions). Updates are provided at joint TSG SA/RAN/CT plenaries, where the latest TR 21.802 draft is reviewed and approved. An extension of six months beyond TSG #111 (March 2026) is currently proposed: There was a proposal to extend the study, with a clear preference from many companies for an extension rather than concluding in March 2026. A 6-month extension was considered more reasonable than a 3-month one, given PCG timing. Any extension would require SID revision and approval at TSG#111 and would be used to develop and trial concrete, reproducible working solutions (e.g. via playgrounds and limited real-meeting trials).
